children.text: Known as the "Boracay of the North," Pagudpud is a beach town at the very northern tip of Luzon. From the fine white sands of Saud Beach to Blue Lagoon, a favorite with surfers, to Kabigan Falls hidden in the jungle and the cliff-hugging Patapat Viaduct, it offers a quiet, laid-back getaway.
Pagudpud is a beach town in the far north of Ilocos Norte, at the northern tip of Luzon island. It is a long way up the coast road from Laoag, around
2 hours

, but the sea waiting at the end is worth the trip. Saud Beach, with fine white sand curving like a half-moon, shades from transparent turquoise to deep cobalt blue as the water deepens, which is why it has long been nicknamed the "Boracay of the North."
Pagudpud is a municipality split off from Bangui on
February 14, 1954

, a small town of about 194.9 km² with 16 barangays (villages) and a population of 25,565 (2024 census). The coastal highlands to the east were designated the Kalbario–Patapat Natural Park, covering about 3,800 ha, in
, and on Caparispisan Hill to the north stands a wind farm (27 turbines of 3 MW each) that began operating in
. In
, the American travel magazine Travel + Leisure included Saud Beach in its "25 Most Beautiful Beaches in the World," the only Philippine beach on the list.

What sets it apart from Boracay is how quiet it is. Rather than a resort town lined with big hotels and nightlife, this is a peaceful coast dotted with beach resorts under the shade of palm trees. Outside weekends and peak season, you can practically have a stretch of beach to yourself, and at night only the sound of the waves and the stars remain.
The sea isn't all there is, either. Walk about
30 minutes
into the jungle and you'll find Kabigan Falls, over

high, and the Patapat Viaduct, which winds along cliffs above the South China Sea, is one of the Philippines' most celebrated drives. In winter, surfers flock to Blue Lagoon to ride the waves whipped up by the northeast monsoon.

It suits families and couples who want to relax by the sea while adding a bit of waterfall trekking and driving. Since the trip from Laoag is long for a day visit, staying at least one night and touring northern Ilocos together with the Bangui Windmills and Kapurpurawan Rock Formation is recommended.

Pagudpud's signature beach, with fine sand and a gentle slope that make it great for swimming with children. The water is calm and clear in the dry season, but waves rise on windy days, so check the flags on site. The beach stretches about
2 km
, and adults pay a
environmental fee at the entrance to the Saud Municipal Beach Park.

Blue Lagoon, east of Saud Beach, lives up to its name with beautiful blue water, and two rock islets in the sea, "Dos Hermanos," give the view its focal point. The beach is wide, good for strolls and photos. It is about
20–30 minutes
from town by tricycle, and wind turbines line the hill behind the beach.
When the northeast monsoon blows from around
November
to
March
, good surfing waves roll into Blue Lagoon. You can rent a board and take a beginner lesson at the surf shops on the beach.
From the entrance, a walk of about
30 minutes
along rice paddies and a forest trail leads to a waterfall about
high with a cold pool beneath it. You register at the ranger station and go in with a local guide.
A viaduct that runs about
1.3 km
along the cliffs of Pagudpud's east coast, with jungle cliffs on one side and the South China Sea on the other. You can stop at the roadside viewpoints to take photos. It is about another
15 minutes
by car from the Kabigan Falls entrance, and the structure of the bridge and its viewpoints are covered in detail in the
Patapat Viaduct
entry.
A small roadside spring and shrine near the Patapat Viaduct, said to bring good fortune to those who drink its water. The cold, clear spring water is a refreshing way to beat the heat for a moment.

A distinctive formation with a hole through the middle of a seaside hill; its name means "mountain with a hole" in Ilocano. Climbing the steps, the sea view through the opening is striking. It lies on the coast of Balaoi, the same village as Kabigan Falls, so it is usually visited together on northern tours.

Direct buses run from Manila to Pagudpud. According to the Pagudpud municipal guide, Partas, GV Florida and RCJ buses serve this route, with air-conditioned, deluxe and sleeper buses available. GV Florida runs a deluxe bus to Pagudpud and Laoag from its Sampaloc terminal at

10–12 hours

If the direct times don't suit you, go as far as
Laoag
and transfer. Partas, Fariñas, GV Florida, Maria de Leon and others run dozens of Manila–Laoag buses a day, taking about
9–11 hours
, with fares of roughly
depending on class.

Pagudpud lies on the route where the Manila North Road, which climbs the northwest coast of Luzon, crosses the Patapat Viaduct into Cagayan province. For this reason, GV Florida and GMW buses linking Laoag with Aparri, Santa Ana and Tuguegarao in Cagayan pass through here, and you can simply ask to be dropped off where you like. From the GV Florida Santa Ana terminal, buses toward Laoag, Vigan and Baguio leave at
and
, so they work for an itinerary that visits
Palaui Island
before crossing over to Pagudpud. It takes about
4–5 hours
from Santa Ana to Pagudpud.
It is about
558 km

from Manila to Pagudpud. Take the NLEX, SCTEX and TPLEX expressways up toward Pangasinan and La Union, then keep heading north on the Manila North Road along the coast through Vigan and Laoag; with rest stops, the drive takes about
10–12 hours
. From Laoag to Pagudpud is about
72 km
. Parking at the Saud Municipal Beach Park costs
for a car and
for a bus or truck (up to 10 hours,
for each additional hour).
From Laoag city, a bus or van toward Pagudpud and Claveria takes about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours 30 minutes
, with fares of roughly
. From Pagudpud town (the poblacion) to Saud Beach is about
15 minutes
by tricycle and to Blue Lagoon about
20–30 minutes
, with short rides starting from
per person. The northern tricycle tour that covers Kabigan Falls, Bantay Abot Cave, the Patapat Viaduct and Blue Lagoon, and the southern tour that covers the Bangui Windmills and Burgos, cost about
per tricycle (up to 3 people) and can be arranged through your resort or at the tricycle stand in town. The driver often doubles as a tour guide.
The best time for swimming is from
March
to
May
. The wind dies down during this period, so the sea is calm and the water is at its clearest. However, resorts fill up quickly during Holy Week and the
May
holidays, when domestic travelers flock in, so book ahead.
From
December
to
February

is still the dry season, but the strong northeast monsoon means waves are often high. This period suits surfing and beach walks more than swimming, and mornings and evenings are cool. The surfing season generally runs from
November–March
From
June
to
October
is the rainy season, and typhoons are frequent in northern Luzon from
July–September
. When a typhoon hits, the Patapat Viaduct section may be closed due to landslide risk, and buses can stop running. Resort rates drop in the off-season, but keep in mind the weather is a real gamble.
Pagudpud receives about 1,985 mm of rain a year, concentrated in
June–September
, with about 112 rainy days a year. Daytime temperatures are hot all year, around
. Every
February 14
, on its founding anniversary, the town holds a fair-like celebration.

Lodging is concentrated in two areas, Saud Beach and Blue Lagoon. Saud Beach has fine sand and is close to restaurants and amenities, making it convenient for families visiting for the first time, with beachfront resort rooms priced around

per night. Blue Lagoon has a wider, quieter beach, home to Hannah's Beach Resort, a long-established large property, along with mid-range resorts and budget lodging for surfers. Guesthouses along the town and roadside go for around
per night.

Saud Beach has a cluster of long-established beachfront lodgings such as Saud Beach Resort & Hotel, Evangeline Beach Resort and Apo Idon Beach Hotel, and Kapuluan Vista Resort is on the Blue Lagoon side. If you only want to enjoy the beach without staying overnight, you can rent a cottage at the Saud Municipal Beach Park for
a day. The Tourist Rest Area at Saud Beach has a pasalubong (souvenir) shop selling Ilocos regional products, a good place to pick up gifts on your way home.

Most meals are had at resort restaurants. Bagnet and pinakbet, the classic Ilocano dishes, along with fish and squid grilled over charcoal that day, and shrimp sinigang (a tangy soup), are the staples. Small beachside eateries sell fresh coconut juice and halo-halo, while the town market offers cheap local meals. Pagudpud also does seafood cured in coconut vinegar well, so a seafood dinner with kilawin (vinegar-cured ceviche) is a popular choice.
Pagudpud has very few ATMs, and cash withdrawal often fails. Bring enough cash from Laoag to cover your expenses beyond accommodation.
Some resorts don't accept card payments. Check the payment method when you book.
Phone signal reaches most beach resorts, but weakens near the falls and along the Patapat stretch.
The path to Kabigan Falls crosses rice paddies and streams, so aqua shoes or trekking sandals are comfortable.
Saud Beach photos come out with the clearest water color in the morning light. Blue Lagoon is beautiful at sunset with the Dos Hermanos rock islets in silhouette.
The last bus from Laoag to Pagudpud often stops running in the late afternoon. On your return day, depart before
Resorts fill up early during Holy Week and the
May
and
December
holidays. Book at least 2–3 weeks in advance.
Beach trash bins can be scarce, so it's a good idea to bring a small trash bag and take your own litter with you.
At Saud Beach there is a Tourist Rest Area opened by the Department of Tourism in
May 2024
. It has restrooms and tourist information facilities, making it a good place to rest for a while during a northern tour.
The environmental fee, cottage and parking rates at Saud Municipal Beach Park are set by Pagudpud Ordinance No. 2025-039. In
July 2026
, a claim spread on social media of a "2-hour entrance fee of
," but that was actually the daily cottage rental. If a charge seems odd, check at the beach park information desk and get a receipt.
During the strong northeast monsoon from
November–February
, waves and rip currents get stronger. Avoid swimming on beaches without a lifeguard, and never go in when a red flag is up.
Kabigan Falls is closed when water levels rise during the rainy season. The rocks below the falls are slippery, so don't attempt reckless dives.
During typhoon season, there is a risk of falling rocks and landslides around the Patapat Viaduct. Follow any traffic control notices.
During Super Typhoon Nando (international name Ragasa) in
September 2025

, a state of calamity was declared in Pagudpud and 631 homes were damaged. If you visit in the rainy season, check the PAGASA typhoon forecasts and Pagudpud municipal announcements, and leave a spare day in your schedule in case roads are cut off.
Confirm the fare and what's included in advance for tricycle tours and surf lessons.
The sun is very strong. Reef-safe sunscreen and a rash guard are recommended.
Most Pagudpud beaches have no lifeguard on duty. On days with high waves, staying no deeper than ankle level is the safest choice.
